args.doc: Bullets in one pull. Default 1. A shotgunner is 3.
args.name: count

args.doc: Degrees of random cone, per bullet.
args.name: spread

args.doc: Tracer style to draw, or absent for none.
args.name: tracer

args.doc: World units per second, away from the muzzle. PER RAY.
args.name: knockback

args.doc: A particle kind to burst where this lands, by catalogue id. Drawn entirely by the client -- nothing about it crosses the wire or enters a hash.
args.name: hit_vfx

args.doc: How wide a volume the burst comes out of. A blast wants its own radius here so the particles fill it rather than all starting at one point.
args.name: hit_vfx_radius

args.doc: Multiplier on the target's move_speed. Needs `slow_ticks`.
args.name: slow

actions.doc: An instant shot. The engine answers where the ray ended and what was there; what that COSTS is this action.
actions.name: hitscan

args.doc: Degrees between shots when `count` > 1. A mancubus volley.
args.name: arc

args.doc: How far in front of the body it appears. Launched clear or it is touching its owner on the tick it exists.
args.name: offset

actions.doc: Launch one of the `missiles` defined in the same file.
actions.name: missile

actions.doc: Hurt the current target, with no range test. For a missile's `on_hit`, where contact has ALREADY been established by the flight -- `melee` measures from the actor, and a missile's actor is the mob that fired it, which by then is somewhere else entirely. That was a real bug: a fireball burst on the player and did nothing, because the range was being tested from twelve units back where the imp was standing.
actions.name: damage

actions.doc:
Start the swept collider this mob declares in its `swing` field. ONE TICK is all this does: the engine's attack is edge-triggered, so the press starts a swing that then runs for `ticks` on its own and hits each target at most once however long it lasts.
A mob with no `swing` field does nothing here and says so at load, rather than swinging with the engine's defaults -- which would be a two-unit reach nobody asked for.
actions.name: swing

args.doc: Which warning to draw, by catalogue id.
args.name: effect

args.doc: How long until the blow lands -- the number a player needs in order to decide whether to move.
args.name: ticks

actions.doc:
ANNOUNCE AN INCOMING ATTACK so a client can warn about it. Put one at `at = 0` of an attack state and the blow later in the same sequence; the gap between them IS the player's reaction time, and writing it as two entries is what makes it tunable.
No wire format of its own: it rides the vfx event, radius in 1/256 units in the low sixteen bits of `param` and ticks in the high sixteen.
actions.name: telegraph

args.doc: World units per second, away from the attacker.
args.name: knockback

args.doc: A particle kind to burst where this lands. A mob's own `blood` overrides it.
args.name: hit_vfx

actions.doc: Damage if the target is inside `range` right now. Separate from `hitscan` because a monster with only a ranged attack is harmless the moment you stand inside it -- a missile spawned inside somebody bursts on its owner or sails past.
actions.name: melee

args.doc: Degrees of random slop on the direction.
args.name: jitter

actions.doc: A shove, in world units per second. A lost soul's charge, a leap.
actions.name: impulse

args.doc: Refuse if this many of that kind are already alive and owned by this one. A pain elemental without a budget fills the entity table.
args.name: limit

args.doc: Scatter each child within this radius. A spawner without one stacks its brood on a single point, where they spend their first second pushing each other apart.
args.name: jitter

args.doc: Only this kind. Absent means any.
args.name: mob

actions.doc: Put a corpse in reach back on its feet. Costs no engine support: corpses are already a script-side list.
actions.name: revive

args.doc: Outward from the blast CENTRE, not from the mob.
args.name: knockback

args.doc: A particle kind to burst where this lands, by catalogue id. Drawn entirely by the client -- nothing about it crosses the wire or enters a hash.
args.name: hit_vfx

args.doc: How wide a volume the burst comes out of. A blast wants its own radius here so the particles fill it rather than all starting at one point.
args.name: hit_vfx_radius

actions.doc: A blast. `hurts_owner` false is a rocket that does not kill the cyberdemon that fired it.
actions.name: damage_area

args.doc: Up to this many extra ticks, rolled here. Two monsters that started together stop firing in unison.
args.name: jitter

actions.doc: Writes tick + ticks into the var, for `cooldown_ready` to read.
actions.name: set_cooldown

actions.doc: Roll a number into a variable, inclusive at both ends. With `var_at_least` this is weighted branching, which a single `chance` cannot express: roll once, then let several transitions read the same roll rather than each rolling its own.
actions.name: var_random

actions.doc: Leave now, mid-sequence. The rest of the sequence does not run.
actions.name: goto

args.doc: Degrees, an ABSOLUTE world heading, for `towards = angle`. 0 is +x and it counts anticlockwise, which is what dnp.atan2 answers in.
args.name: angle

args.doc: A per-mob variable holding a heading, for `towards = var`. Written by `set_angle`, which is how a mob turns to something it worked out earlier.
args.name: var

args.doc: Degrees added after, signed. `towards = target` with an offset of 90 is a monster sidling across your front rather than walking into it.
args.name: offset

args.doc: Degrees of random slop either side, added last. Draws once, off the world's own stream, exactly as `chance` does -- so it replays.
args.name: jitter

actions.doc: Turn to face, once, at this instant. Doom's A_FaceTarget, and the reason a monster's shot goes where you are rather than where you were when it started winding up.
actions.name: face

args.doc: Degrees, for `towards = angle`.
args.name: angle

args.doc: Degrees of random slop either side.
args.name: jitter

actions.doc:
Work out a heading and keep it in a variable, for `face` and for `move = "wander"` to read.
AN ANGLE IS A NUMBER, so it lives in the same per-mob variables everything else does rather than in a second kind of storage: a turn is 2^32 and that is exact in a double, which is why brad are plain Lua numbers here and `homing` on a missile is an int.
`towards = random` is the one that makes wandering wander. Without it `move = "wander"` reads a heading nothing ever wrote and walks straight at the aim -- which it did, silently, for as long as the mode has existed.
actions.name: set_angle

actions.doc: A replicated movement parameter, by the name in core/include/dnp/physics/params_table.hpp. This is how a mob changes its own speed -- and because the parameter replicates, every client agrees without this file knowing the wire exists.
actions.name: set_param

args.doc: A name this modifier REPLACES rather than stacks on. Two `effect` actions with the same tag on the same entity leave one effect, not two -- which is what a weapon writing its own reach needs, since switching weapons ten times would otherwise leave ten reaches multiplied together. Without a tag they stack, which is what a stack of buffs wants.
args.name: tag

actions.doc: A temporary modifier through the effect stack, which recomputes from base every tick and so cannot drift.
actions.name: effect

args.doc: For a PARTICLE kind: how wide a volume the burst comes out of. A blast whose specks all start at one point reads as a firecracker however many there are.
args.name: radius

actions.doc: Fire a visual effect. `at = "impact"` is what an explosion wants: it draws where the missile LANDED, and it draws whether or not anything was in range -- unlike `hit_vfx` on damage_area, which is per victim and so shows nothing at all when a rocket hits an empty wall.
actions.name: vfx

args.doc: The sound's name in the module's bank (`monster.imp.sight`). A name the bank does not have is silence, said once by the client.
args.name: name

args.doc: Where it is heard from -- not `at`, which in a sequence is WHEN. `self` (the default) follows the mob as it moves; `impact` is where a missile landed, for its burst.
args.name: from

actions.doc: Play a sound. Heard by everybody near it, and never the only sign of anything: a sound may be dropped, a hit may not.
actions.name: sound

actions.doc: Override the state's own `anim` mid-sequence.
actions.name: set_anim

args.doc: Default 'player', which is what the runtime does on its own.
args.name: of

args.doc: How far to look. Absent means the mob's own `sight`.
args.name: distance

args.doc: Only this kind, when looking for a mob.
args.name: mob

args.doc: Only this record, when looking for a prop.
args.name: prop

args.doc: Require a clear ray. Costs one per candidate, so put a `distance` on it.
args.name: visible

actions.doc: Point this mob at the nearest thing that matches, or at nothing if none does.
actions.name: target_nearest

actions.doc: Turn on whatever last hurt it. The mob-level `infighting` field does this automatically and unconditionally; this is how a graph decides for itself -- retaliate only below half health, or only when the attacker is closer than what it is already chasing.
actions.name: target_attacker

args.doc: Wake every dormant mob within this far as well. Absent wakes only itself.
args.name: radius

args.doc: Only this kind, when a radius is given.
args.name: mob

actions.doc: Stop being dormant. `dormant` is set when a mob is placed and until now nothing could change it -- so an ambush was a room of monsters that either all started awake or never woke at all.
actions.name: wake

actions.doc: Go dormant: no decisions, no movement, no cost beyond existing. What a spawner's children do until the fight reaches them.
actions.name: sleep

args.doc: Only this kind. Absent means any.
args.name: mob

actions.doc: Hand this mob's target to everything near it, waking what is dormant. Doom's noise propagation, which is most of why a room reacts as a room -- without it a mob only ever learns about you by seeing you itself.
actions.name: alert_nearby

actions.doc: Forget the current target. `has_target` is then false and the runtime will acquire again on a later think.
actions.name: target_none

actions.doc: The escape hatch. `mob` is in scope, and so is everything in dnp.*. Anything this vocabulary cannot say goes here, and that is what it is for -- a framework whose only extension point is adding to the framework is one nobody can build on.
actions.name: lua

conditions.doc: Something is being hunted at all.
conditions.name: has_target

conditions.doc: Plan distance, not 3D: a cacodemon above you is still near you.
conditions.name: target_within

conditions.doc: A ray reaches it. NOT the same question as `target_within`, and conflating them is what had monsters shooting through two walls at somebody across the map. The target is a COLUMN and not a point: a body whose head is over a ledge your eyeline runs under is visible, and asking only about its middle is what had monsters forgetting a player standing higher or lower than them. Costs a raycast -- put a `target_within` before it.
conditions.name: target_visible

args.doc: Degrees either side of facing. Default 90.
args.name: arc

conditions.doc: Whether the target is within the arc the mob is facing.
conditions.name: target_in_front

conditions.doc: Of its own starting hp.
conditions.name: hp_below

conditions.doc: How long it has been in the current state.
conditions.name: state_elapsed

conditions.doc: Rolls dnp.random, which is seeded per world and replays identically. The ONLY condition that is not a pure read; it is here rather than in `lua` because refire, wander and pain all want it and none of them should have to compile a chunk.
conditions.name: chance

conditions.doc: A per-mob counter.
conditions.name: var_at_least

conditions.doc: The named var holds an absolute tick; true once it has passed. A deadline rather than a counter, so a mob nobody is near is not paying to tick one down.
conditions.name: cooldown_ready

args.doc: Ticks. Default 1 -- this tick.
args.name: within

conditions.doc: Something damaged it recently. The pain-state edge.
conditions.name: was_hurt

args.doc: Only this kind. Absent means any mob at all.
args.name: mob

args.doc: Default true. False finds corpses, which is what a resurrector wants to look for before it commits to the animation.
args.name: alive

conditions.doc: Another mob is within reach. Itself never counts.
conditions.name: mob_within

args.doc: Only this catalogue record. Absent means any prop.
args.name: prop

conditions.doc: A prop is within reach -- a barrel to shoot, a totem to guard, a key somebody dropped. Props are not mobs and have no graph; this is how a brain notices the furniture.
conditions.name: prop_within

conditions.doc: At least this many mobs of that kind are within reach. A monster that only charges in a group, or one that panics alone.
conditions.name: count_within

conditions.doc:
A route to the target exists for a body this size. A monster that cannot get to you should give up and do something else rather than press into the wall between you forever -- which is what `move = chase` does, indefinitely, with nothing reporting it.
COSTS AN A* and the engine refuses past sixty-four a tick, so a level of monsters all asking on the same tick would have most of them silently answered no. Put a `target_within` in front of it and a `cooldown_ready` beside it.
conditions.name: can_reach

args.doc: Degrees either side of facing. Default 12 -- the width a shot actually occupies, not a field of view.
args.name: arc

args.doc: How far to look. Default the mob's own sight.
args.name: distance

args.doc: Only this kind counts as an ally. Absent means any mob, which is usually what is meant.
args.name: mob

conditions.doc: Another mob is standing in the line this one would shoot along. In Doom hitting it is a FEATURE -- infighting is most of what makes a crowded room interesting -- so this is not wired in anywhere by default. It is here for everything that is not Doom, where a squad that shoots its own back is a bug.
conditions.name: ally_in_front

args.doc: How much higher it has to be. Default zero.
args.name: by

conditions.doc: The target's feet are above this mob's by at least `by`. A flyer matching height, or a melee monster declining to swing at somebody on a balcony -- reach is a 3D question and `target_within` deliberately is not.
conditions.name: target_above

conditions.doc: The other way round.
conditions.name: target_below

args.doc: How long it must have been getting nowhere. Default 16 -- two of its own decisions.
args.name: ticks

conditions.doc:
It has been trying to move and has not. The classic monster grinding into a corner -- pathing gets it near, geometry stops it, and nothing in the graph can tell, because `move = chase` looks identical whether it is working or not.
ONE NUMBER, and the distance is not a second: the runtime keeps an anchor and moves it whenever the body gets a quarter unit away, so `ticks` is how long that anchor has stood still. The first version took a distance too and could never be true -- the anchor was rewritten every think, so the window it measured was always exactly one think long.
conditions.name: stuck

conditions.doc: What it is currently hunting. Since `target_nearest` can point a mob at something that is not a player, a graph that cares has to be able to ask.
conditions.name: target_is

conditions.doc: What hurt it was another mob, not a player. The infighting edge.
conditions.name: hurt_by_mob

args.doc: An expression over `mob`, returning truthy.
args.name: code

args.doc: A Lua function taking `mob`. Needs no compiler at run time, so it works under Trust::Strict where `code` does not.
args.name: fn

conditions.doc: The escape hatch. Anything the vocabulary cannot say.
conditions.name: lua

drop_choice_fields.doc: A catalogue name, or absent for nothing.
drop_choice_fields.name: item

drop_choice_fields.doc: Its share against the others' weights, at least 1.
drop_choice_fields.name: weight

drop_fields.doc: A catalogue name (assets/props.txt): placed at the body, every time.
drop_fields.name: item

drop_fields.doc: How many of it, or of what `one_of` picks. Defaults to 1; spread round the body so they do not stack in one spot.
drop_fields.name: count

drop_fields.doc: A list of weighted choices (see drop_choice_fields), ONE of which drops. A choice with no `item` is nothing, which is how a drop is made a chance: { {item = 'medikit', weight = 1}, {weight = 3} } is a medikit one time in four.
drop_fields.name: one_of

missile_fields.doc: Which catalogue record this missile is drawn from, and whose radius it hits with. Defaults to the missile's own name, as a mob's does.
missile_fields.name: prop

missile_fields.doc: What it collides with, as a radius. Absent means the `prop`'s own radius from assets/props.txt, which is usually right -- a missile that hits with a different size than it is drawn is a missile players learn to distrust.
missile_fields.name: radius

missile_fields.doc: How far above the shooter's feet it appears. Doom launches from mid-body; a missile born at ankle height clips the first step it crosses.
missile_fields.name: z_offset

missile_fields.doc: Zero for a Doom fireball, which flies flat. Nonzero for a grenade.
missile_fields.name: gravity

missile_fields.doc: Ticks before it expires on its own. A missile with no ceiling on its life leaks a prop slot per shot.
missile_fields.name: life

missile_fields.doc:
Degrees per tick it may turn towards its target. A revenant's missile. Absent means it flies straight.
An INT, not an fx: angles here are brad -- a turn is 2^32 -- and brad is a plain Lua number, because 2^32 is exact in a double. Declaring it `fx` made it an fx userdata that then met plain arithmetic and raised.
missile_fields.name: homing

missile_fields.doc: Runs when it reaches something, with the thing it reached as the target. This is where the damage and the splash go -- so a rocket is a missile whose on_hit is a damage_area, and nothing in the runtime knows what a rocket is.
missile_fields.name: on_hit

mob_fields.doc: Which catalogue record is this mob's BODY. Defaults to the mob's own name, which is what you want: a mob and its body are one thing said in two files, and restating the name in the second one is how they come to disagree. assets/props.txt owns the radius, height, speed, solid flag and the sprites, because the client reads that file too. NOTHING in THIS file crosses the wire: a client that needed a pain chance to draw a monster would be a protocol leak. Name a record here only to make two mobs share one body deliberately.
mob_fields.name: prop

mob_fields.doc: The engine has no notion of health. This is the script's.
mob_fields.name: hp

mob_fields.doc: Which state a freshly spawned mob enters. Defaults to the first state in declaration order.
mob_fields.name: initial

mob_fields.doc: Per-mob counters, by name, with their starting values. Each mob gets its own copy at spawn. This is where a refire count, a spawn budget or a grudge lives.
mob_fields.name: vars

mob_fields.doc: How far this mob notices a target at all. A cheap distance gate checked before anything expensive -- `target_visible` casts a ray, and a ray for every monster on a Doom level every tick is the cost this exists to avoid.
mob_fields.name: sight

mob_fields.doc: 0-255, rolled when the mob is hurt: the chance it flinches at all. Doom's number, because it is a good one -- a monster that ALWAYS flinches can be stun-locked, and one that never does gives no feedback that a hit landed.
mob_fields.name: pain_chance

mob_fields.doc: Turns per second the body may rotate. The engine's default is 4, which is a quarter of a second to come ninety degrees -- and a monster fires along the direction its BODY is pointing, not the one it is aiming at, so a body that lags its target wastes shots into the nearest wall. In a corridor a few degrees off is a wall a metre away, which is what a tracer that renders as a stub is showing you.
mob_fields.name: turn_speed

mob_fields.doc:
How much MORE than a step this mob can gain by hopping. Absent or zero is design §3.2.2's rule -- enemies do not jump -- and routes exactly as it always did.
It is a ROUTING capability and a promise: the nav graph will plan through rises up to this, and the runtime then presses jump where the route says to. Setting it higher than the mob's `jump_impulse` can actually reach gives routes it cannot walk, and the symptom is a monster pressed into a ledge forever.
mob_fields.name: jump_height

mob_fields.doc: Sets gravity_scale to zero at spawn and lets `move` drive Z. Costs no engine support: gravity_scale is a replicated parameter, so a flying monster is flying on every client without a word of it crossing the wire.
mob_fields.name: flying

mob_fields.doc: For a flyer: how far above its target's feet it tries to sit.
mob_fields.name: hover_z

mob_fields.doc: Whether being hurt by another mob makes that mob the target. Doom's monsters do this and it is most of what makes a crowded room interesting.
mob_fields.name: infighting

mob_fields.doc:
THE SWEPT COLLIDER this mob attacks with, if it does -- a volume that moves through an arc over several ticks, so a target that steps out of the way mid-swing is MISSED. The same engine facility a player's melee uses, with the same fields, because a monster's claw and a player's fist are the same thing and there is no reason the player should be the only one who can be dodged.
Distinct from the `melee` action, which is an instant distance test: that hits whatever is in range on the tick it runs and nothing can be done about it. Declare this and put a `swing` action in the attack state's sequence. See swing_fields.
mob_fields.name: swing

mob_fields.doc:
The particle kind this mob sprays when it is hurt, by catalogue id. OVERRIDES whatever the attack named, because what bleeds is the target's business: an imp bleeds green whether it was shot, punched or blown up, and the alternative is every weapon in every module listing every exception.
Absent takes the attack's own `hit_vfx`, which is how everything that is not an exception stays red.
mob_fields.name: blood

mob_fields.doc: Whether the body stays after the death state's sequence ends. Corpses are capped and recycled oldest-first by the runtime.
mob_fields.name: corpse

mob_fields.doc: How hard this mob is to shove, Doom's way: a knockback is divided by mass / 100, so 100 (the default, a zombieman or a player) takes it whole and a baron's 1000 a tenth of it.
mob_fields.name: mass

mob_fields.doc: What this mob leaves where it dies: a LIST of entries (see drop_fields), each either an `item` that always drops or a `one_of` weighted choice, which can include nothing. Rolled on the server the moment it dies, so every client sees one outcome. An item is a catalogue name, picked up like any other: a dropped clip gives a clip's worth, not Doom's half.
mob_fields.name: drops

state_fields.doc: The animation state number the client already understands -- the `state <n>` on a sprite line in assets/props.txt. The server declares it and the client owns the timing (design §4), so this is a number, not a frame list.
state_fields.name: anim

state_fields.doc: How the body is driven while in this state. `free` means the state's own actions drive it and the runtime keeps its hands off -- what a scripted leap or a custom controller wants.
state_fields.name: move

state_fields.doc: Where it looks. Separate from `move` because a monster backing away from you while still facing you is a different thing from one turning its back, and Doom's flee does the first.
state_fields.name: face

state_fields.doc: How long the state lasts. Absent means until a transition fires -- which is what `chase` wants and what an attack does not.
state_fields.name: ticks

state_fields.doc: Up to this many EXTRA ticks, rolled on entry. A room of monsters entering the same state on the same tick leaves it on the same tick and moves as one animal, which reads as a bug even when every one of them is behaving. Needs `ticks`; without one there is no duration to lengthen.
state_fields.name: ticks_jitter

state_fields.doc: Where it goes when `ticks` runs out. Absent with `ticks` set is a state that ends and stays, which the loader refuses.
state_fields.name: next

state_fields.doc: Ordered {at = <ticks after entry>, ...action}. `at` is relative to entering the state and is a DEADLINE, not a countdown: a mob nobody is near costs nothing between its own decisions.
state_fields.name: sequence

state_fields.doc: Ordered { to = <state>, when = {conditions} }. FIRST MATCH WINS, and order is the priority -- there is no scoring and no backtracking, because a graph whose behaviour depends on a weighting nobody can see is not one an editor can show you.
state_fields.name: transitions

state_fields.doc: Whether pain and death may cut this state short. Death ignores it; nothing interrupts dying.
state_fields.name: interruptible

state_fields.doc: Collision while in this state. A corpse sets it false, which is why you can walk over one.
state_fields.name: solid

swing_fields.doc: What a connected swing costs. SCRIPT, not a parameter -- putting damage in the replicated table would hand the client the numbers to compute it with.
swing_fields.name: damage

swing_fields.doc: To the target's SURFACE, not its centre.
swing_fields.name: reach

swing_fields.doc: How wide, either side of the aim. 0.125 is 45 degrees each way. A narrow arc is a lunge you can side-step; a wide one sweeps the room and is what a big monster should have.
swing_fields.name: half_arc

swing_fields.doc: Where the collider starts, relative to the aim.
swing_fields.name: sweep_from

swing_fields.doc: And where it ends. Equal values make a THRUST that does not rotate -- a spear, a horn, a charge.
swing_fields.name: sweep_to

swing_fields.doc: The INNER edge, as a distance from the body's surface. Non-zero makes a ring segment that misses anything pressed against the body, so getting inside the weapon's reach is how you beat it. On a monster this is the parameter that makes closing the distance the right answer rather than the fatal one.
swing_fields.name: min_reach

swing_fields.doc: How long the collider is live, and the whole reason this is worth having: with a duration the swing can be READ and dodged. Zero is re-read as one by the engine, which is an instant hit.
swing_fields.name: ticks

swing_fields.doc: Ticks before another swing may START. Capped at 255 by the parameter's width. A mob's state graph usually gates this already; set it when two states could both swing.
swing_fields.name: cooldown

swing_fields.doc: Where the collider starts VERTICALLY, as a turn fraction: 0 is level, 0.25 straight up, -0.25 straight down.
swing_fields.name: pitch_from

swing_fields.doc: And where it ends. A cyberdemon bringing a hoof down runs from above to level; equal values are a fixed elevation.
swing_fields.name: pitch_to

swing_fields.doc: How tall the arc is, either side of the pitch. ABSENT OR ZERO MEANS NO VERTICAL CHECK -- bounded only by the body's height, which is how every swing behaved before pitch existed. Set it and an overhead blow genuinely misses something at your feet.
swing_fields.name: half_pitch

swing_fields.doc: How hard a connected swing throws the target, in world units per second, directly away from the swinger.
swing_fields.name: knockback

swing_fields.doc: A particle kind to burst where this lands, by catalogue id. Drawn entirely by the client -- nothing about it crosses the wire or enters a hash.
swing_fields.name: hit_vfx

swing_fields.doc: How wide a volume the burst comes out of. A blast wants its own radius here so the particles fill it rather than all starting at one point.
swing_fields.name: hit_vfx_radius

swing_fields.doc: The vertical part of that shove.
swing_fields.name: lift

swing_fields.doc: Multiplier on the target's move_speed while it lasts. Needs `slow_ticks` beside it or nothing happens.
swing_fields.name: slow

swing_fields.doc: How long the slow lasts. Tagged by the attacker, so hitting the same target twice REPLACES rather than stacking to a standstill.
swing_fields.name: slow_ticks
